    The fixed-cohook Figure 55 backward walk #

    Package the two local path replacements of BGRS Figure 55 into a decreasing rho-index state while comparing every candidate with one fixed efficient cohook tackle.

    source
    theorem LargeIndecomposable.RayCohookTackle.rho_zero_not_isIso {C : Type u} [CategoryTheory.Category.{v, u} C] [CategoryTheory.Limits.HasZeroMorphisms C] {m : ℕ} (t : RayCohookTackle m) :
    ¬CategoryTheory.IsIso ↑(t.rho 0)

    The first rho of a cohook tackle lies in its first peak and is therefore noninvertible.

    source
    theorem LargeIndecomposable.RayCohookTackle.efficiency_lex_pair_of_rho_zero_depth_lt {C : Type u} [CategoryTheory.Category.{v, u} C] [CategoryTheory.Limits.HasZeroMorphisms C] [HasFiniteRayPathDepth C] {m : ℕ} (t : RayCohookTackle m) {a b : ℕ} (h : (t.rho 0).depth < a) :
    List.Lex (fun (r s : ℕ) => r < s) t.efficiency [a, b]

    Increasing the first rho depth strictly increases a cohook efficiency word, independently of the remaining singleton-candidate entry.

      Nonempty (Figure55CohookRhoStage t p q (Fin.last m))

      An essential occurrence of the final cohook with nonidentity context on both sides produces the initial rho-stage. Efficiency rules out the direct compatible hook extension, so the occurrence remainder factors through the last rho; the factor is noninvertible and supplies the positive right path.

      False

      The dual opening contradiction when the quiver suffix is the identity. The selected cohook itself is source-incomparable with the other contour side's final arrow, so appending that arrow gives an efficiency word which strictly extends the original word after the same final depth.

      o.before.length = 0

      Source-faithful dual of BGRS 8.4 for an efficient cohook tackle. Duality interchanges the source's prefix and suffix; after reversing the ray quiver, the occurrence's quiver prefix must therefore be an identity path.
